chapters.title: Dress Code
chapters.text:
- Employees are expected to present a neat and well‐groomed appearance in keeping with SCPL's image. This is especially true for those who interact with customers, government authorities and business partners.
- For male staff jacket, formal shirt and trousers are acceptable office attire while flip‐ flops, sandals, sneakers, T‐shirts, jeans and shorts are not acceptable. All chemists shall ware white apron and all other employees shall wear dress code as defined by the management from, time to time.
- For female employees, national dress code (Saree or Punjabi dress) is acceptable while revealing clothes, flip‐flops and sandals are not acceptable clothing. All clothing and jeweler should reflect a professional image.
- For employees who work onsite in the plant, a more casual/SCPL dress code is acceptable provided that it meets EHS and GMP requirements

chapters.title: Confidentiality
Bribery
chapters.text:
In accordance with Saptagir Camphor Private Limited’s Business Ethics Policy no SCPL employee can be involved with either making or accepting bribes, kickbacks or similar transactions.
## Recognizing Bribery
Bribery can take many forms but it usually involves:
- Giving another person an unjustified reward to influence the behavior of that person;
- Receiving a reward from either an individual or a SCPL to influence a decision, or in return, providing a commercial advantage;
- Making, offering or promising to make a payment or to transfer anything of value, including the provision of any service, gift or entertainment, for the purpose of obtaining or retaining a business advantage;
- Making, offering or promising to make such improper payments through third parties;
- Offering or receiving money (or anything of value), gifts, kickbacks or commissions, in relation to obtaining business or awarding contracts;
- Permitting an agent or representative of SCPL to do something that would be unacceptable if undertaken by SCPL personnel;
- Failing to report any indication of improper payments
## Anti‐bribery Laws
A breach of anti‐bribery laws is a serious offense, which can result in fines for companies and imprisonment for individuals. Even the appearance of a breach of anti‐bribery or anti‐corruption laws could do incalculable damage to SCPL’s reputation
## Commissions
Any commissions, payments, or favorable terms arranged by an employee conducting SCPL business shall be in accordance with established policies and shall be promptly recorded in writing.
## Gifts, Entertainment and Favors
## General
Exchanging small gifts and entertainment can build goodwill in a business relationship, but some gifts can result in a situation where improper influences or the appearance of improper influence can have a negative impact on SCPL
## Definition
Gifts, entertainment and favors include the giving or receiving anything of value: e.g. discounts, loans, favorable terms on any product or service, services, prizes, transportation, free courses, use of another SCPL’s vehicles, use of vacation facilities, stocks or other securities, participation in stock offerings, home improvements, holiday tickets, and gift certificates
## Gift Categories
- Those that are usually acceptable and that you may approve yourself;
- Those that may be acceptable but require prior approval; and
- Those that are never acceptable
- Self‐Approval Test for Accepting Gifts
- Intent ‐‐ Is the intent of the gift only to build a business relationship or is it intended to influence your objectivity in making a business decision?
- Materiality ‐‐ Is the gift modest and infrequent or could it place you under an obligation?
- Legality ‐‐ Is the gift or entertainment legal both in your country and in the country of the other party?
- Compliance ‐‐ Is the gift allowed by the recipient’s organization?
- Transparency ‐‐ Would you be embarrassed if your manager, colleagues or anyone outside SCPL became aware of the gift?
## Acceptable Gifts
Some gifts and entertainment are sufficiently modest that they do not require prior approval. Subject to applying the ‘self‐approval test’ the following are usually acceptable for SCPL employees without prior approval:
- Modest occasional meals with someone with whom we do business; or
- Gifts of nominal value, such as pens, calendars, books, souvenirs, tokens, ties, or small promotional items with a less value acceptable to management;
- In addition to applying the principles above, employees should use the self‐approval test to determine whether a gift is appropriate and may be accepted without prior approval
## Gifts Requiring Approval
In determining whether to approve something in this category, managers will apply the criteria described in the ‘self‐approval test’ above
Employees must receive prior written approval from their reporting manager, HR and/or Management when it crosses the acceptable gift category.
- Employees who are offered gifts that exceed acceptable gifts in value (other than cash, money orders, etc.) may accept them, but they must report them immediately to the HR Department for the following:
- May be retained by the recipient;
- Will be retained for the benefit of SCPL;
- Will be sold and the money donated to charity; or
- Will be returned to the offerer of the gift.
- In making the decision, HR Department must take cultural considerations into account, as it may be offensive to return gifts. If it is decided that the gift may be accepted, the recipient should send a brief letter of acknowledgement to the offerer of the gift.
- If it is decided that the gift may not be accepted but it would be considered culturally appropriate to return the gift, then the recipient should contact the donor with the explanation (preferably given during a telephone conversation with the offerer of the gift) that acceptance of the gift would be contrary to the Code of Conduct
